'''''Amelanchier ovalis''''', commonly known as '''snowy mespilus'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> (a name which is also attached to the related ''[[Amelanchier lamarckii|A. lamarckii]]'') or serviceberry, is a [[deciduous]] shrub in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Rosaceae. Its [[pome]] fruits are edible and can be eaten raw or cooked. The species is native to central and southern [[Europe]], as well as [[North Africa]] and the [[Middle East]].<ref>
 map</ref><ref>Bailey, L.H. & E.Z. Bailey. 1976. Hortus Third i–xiv, 1–1290. MacMillan, New York.</ref><ref>[http://www.tela-botanica.org/bdtfx-nn-4092-description Tela Botanica, Description de Coste, ''Amelanchier vulgaris''] in French</ref>

==Description==
There are 25 species of the genus ''[[Amelanchier]]'' reported from the northern hemisphere, and ''A. ovalis'' is the only naturally occurring species of that genus within Europe.<ref name=":4">{{cite book |last1=Krüssmann |first1=G. |title=Handbuch der Laubgehölze |date=1976 |publisher=Verlag Paul Parey |location=Berlin |edition=2}}</ref> A wide morphological variability has been reported for the flowers and leaves.<ref name=":1" /> There are two subspecies which can be distinguished by the number of chromosomes:
* the diploid (2n=34) ''A. ovalis'' subsp. ''ovalis'' 
* the tetraploid (2n = 68) ''A. ovalis'' subsp. ''embergeri''<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.1983.tb00985.x| title=Contribution à la cytotaxonomie de l'Amelanchier ovalis Medikus (Rosaceae)| year=1983| last1=Favarger| first1=Claude| last2=Stearn| first2=William T.| journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society| volume=87| pages=85–103}}</ref>

''Amelanchier ovalis'' is a thornless, summer-green shrub with an irregular spreading growth.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Siegmund |first1=Seybold |title=Schmeil-Fitschen interaktiv die umfassende Bestimmungs- und Informationsdatenbank der Pflanzenwelt Deutschlands und angrenzender Länder; der Schlüssel zur Pflanzenwelt; mit ausführlicher Begleitbroschüre |date=2002 |publisher=Quelle und Meyer |location=Wiebelsheim |isbn=3-494-01327-6 |edition=1.1 (2.Edition)}}</ref> It reaches heights of {{cvt|3|m|ft|abbr=on}}, rarely {{cvt|5|m|ft|abbr=on}}. The branches are slim and tightly erect in younger growing stages, becoming extended afterwards.

Young shoots are thin and white-haired, older shoots are olive or reddish-brown. The buds have felted hairs which is typical for this species.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Schulz |first1=Bernd |title=Gehölzbestimmung im Winter |date=1999 |publisher=Ulmer |location=Stuttgart (Hohenheim) |isbn=978-3-8001-5074-8}}</ref>
The leaves are round or egg-shaped and reach a length of 2 to 5 cm. The top side of the leaves is bald, the underside initially is hairy, but this is lost throughout the growing season.<ref name=infoflora>{{cite web |title=Amelanchier ovalis Medik. |url=https://www.infoflora.ch/de/flora/amelanchier-ovalis.html |website=infoflora |publisher=infloflora|access-date=2022-11-14 }}</ref>
The white flowers, which are herbaceous, develop lateral and terminal from previous years branches between April and May. The flowers build 3 to 8 erect inflorescences at the end of the shoots.<ref name=":0">{{cite book |last1=Nechwatal |first1=Jan |chapter=Amelanchier ovalis|editor-first1=Bernd |editor-first2=Andreas |editor-first3=Ulla M |editor-first4=Horst |editor-last1=Stimm |editor-last2=Roloff |editor-last3=Lang |editor-last4=Weisgerber |title=Enzyklopädie der Holzgewächse: Handbuch und Atlas der Dendrologie |date=2014 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd |isbn=978-3-527-67851-8 |pages=1–8 |doi=10.1002/9783527678518 |chapter-url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/9783527678518.ehg2003009}}</ref>
[[File:AMELANCHIER OVALIS - SANT JUST - IB-121 (Corner).JPG|thumb|Flowers]]
The fruits are small (1 cm) and spherical, ripening between July and August. When ripe, the fruits become black and contain only a small amount of flesh.<ref name=":4" />
[[File:Amelanchier ovalis3.JPG|thumb|Fruits]]

==Distribution and habitat==
''Amelanchier ovalis'' can be found in prealpine and submediterranean climates reaching from [[wikt:colline|colline]] to sub-alpine zones.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Oberdorfer |first1=Erich |title=Pflanzensoziologische Exkursionsflora für Deutschland und angrenzende Gebiete |date=2001 |publisher=Ulmer |location=Stuttgart |isbn=978-3-8001-3131-0 |page=501 |edition=8}}</ref> The most southern place with recorded plants is in [[Morocco]], the most eastern place is in [[Azerbaijan]] and the [[Caucasus]]. Plants have been observed in the [[Valais]] in [[Switzerland]] at an elevation of {{cvt|2000|m|ft|abbr=on}}, and in the [[Atlas Mountains]] at {{cvt|2800|m|ft|abbr=on}}.<ref name=":1">{{cite book |last1=Schroeder |first1=F.G. |title=Amelanchier. In: Illustrierte Flora von Mitteleuropa, Band IV, Teil 2B |date=1995 |publisher=Blackwell Wissenschafts-Verlag |location=Berlin and Wien |pages=385–404 |edition=2}}</ref>

''A. ovalis'' prefers sunny, dry steep slopes, light oak and pine forests and semi-dry grasslands. It grows well in south-facing positions, on rocks with calcareous substrates.<ref name=":1" />

==Ecology==
''Amelanchier ovalis'' grows in areas which are characterized by moderately dry alternating with moist conditions. It is drought resistant, and is for this reason an [[Bioindicator|indicator species]] for dry conditions. [[Soil pH]] ranges from neutral to alkaline (pH 5.5 - 8.5).<ref name=infoflora/> Therefore, plants are found on limy grounds.<ref name=":0" />

Due to its [[Pioneer species|pioneer]] features, ''Amelanchier ovalis'' is able to establish on nutrient poor and stony substrates, and can stabilize soils. For this reason, this species is used for land restoration, afforestation or reconstruction of habitats.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1080/11263504.2020.1727988 | title=Distribution, ecological role and symbioses of selected shrubby species in the Mediterranean Basin: A review | year=2020 | last1=Lombardo | first1=Emanuela | last2=Bancheva | first2=Svetlana | last3=Domina | first3=Gianniantonio | last4=Venturella | first4=Giuseppe | journal=Plant Biosystems | volume=154 | issue=4 | pages=438–454 | hdl=10447/418458 | s2cid=214032750 | url=https://iris.unipa.it/retrieve/handle/10447/418458/903121/Lombardo%26al2020.pdf |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716210610/https://iris.unipa.it/retrieve/handle/10447/418458/903121/Lombardo%26al2020.pdf| archive-date=2021-07-16 |url-status=live}}</ref>

''Amelanchier ovalis'' is an important food source for different insect species providing nectar. The plants are dependent on insect [[pollination]], because self-pollination is inhibited by early ripening of stamens.<ref name=":0" />

In a higher phenological stage of the plant, when plants have built ripe fruits, they are often eaten by birds or mammals.<ref name=":0" /> Through that, seeds of ''A. ovalis'' are dispersed by these animals. Depending on the location ''A.ovalis'' can propagate vegetatively via root shoots.<ref name=":0" />

==Pathology==
Gall mites of the genus ''[[Eriophyes]]'' and ''[[Aceria]]'' cause damage to buds and calyxes by gall formation on leaves. ''A. ovalis'' can also suffer from [[Browsing (herbivory)|browsing]] by game and grazing livestock.<ref name=":0" /> By contrast, the spotted wing drosophila (''[[Drosophila suzukii]]'') does not infest the fruit of the snowy mespilus.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=Felsenbirne |url=https://www.agroscope.admin.ch/agroscope/de/home/themen/pflanzenbau/obstbau/breitenhof/wildsorten/felsenbirne.html |website=Felsenbirne |publisher=Agroscope |access-date=13 November 2022}}</ref>

''A. ovalis'' can be infested by various species of [[Rust (fungus)|rust fungi]] (e.g. ''Gymnosporangium amelanchieris''), and consequently serves as a host plant. Leaves, shoots, flowers and fruits can be affected. In most cases, the damage is insignificant, and the rust fungus does not threaten the survival of the shrub. However, depending on the type of infestation, fruit set may be reduced. ''A. ovalis'' is also a host plant of the [[fire blight]] pathogen ''Erwinia amylovora'' and is highly susceptible to it. In extreme cases, infection with fire blight can even lead to the death of the shrub.<ref name=":0" />
In very dry years, a weak [[powdery mildew]] infestation could be observed.<ref name=":2" />

==Uses==
''Amelanchier ovalis'' can be used for land restoration and afforestation, thanks to its pioneer features.<ref name=":3">{{cite journal |last1=Moraldi |first1=M. |last2=Falcinelli |first2=F. |title=European amelanchier (Amelanchier ovalis). |journal=Sherwood - Foreste ed Alberi Oggi |date=2000 |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=33–38 |url= http://www.proverde.it/Pubblicazioni/pero%20corvino.pdf|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722130639/http://www.proverde.it/Pubblicazioni/pero%20corvino.pdf|archive-date=2023-07-22 |url-status=live|language=it}} [https://www.rivistasherwood.it/riviste/archivio-bibliografico.html?Idarchivio=463 Abstract in English.]<!-- previous url, now dead https://www.cabdirect.org/cabdirect/abstract/20000609869 --></ref> The berries can be eaten fresh, although they taste rather bland. More often they are processed for jam, compote or spirits.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />
Extracts from twigs, leaves and bark can be used for medicinal purposes, due to their richness in biologically active substances, such as [[polyphenols]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Laksaeva |first1=Elena A. |title=Fruits of plants of Amelanchier genus (Amelanchier Medic) as source of biologically active substances and minerals |journal=I.P. Pavlov Russian Medical Biological Herald |date=2018 |volume=26 |issue=2 |pages=296–304 |doi=10.23888/PAVLOVJ2018262296-304 |url=https://doi.org/10.23888/PAVLOVJ2018262296-304 |access-date=8 November 2022|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":3" />
